title: What happens when Virahanka Fibonacci numbers fill a pyramid?
description: The first three Virahanka Fibonacci numbers, one, two and three, are written in the bottom row of a three row pyramid. The pyramid is filled, its top is read, and the grid is checked against the sequence.
teaching_notes: One idea: a block of the pyramid adds two neighbours, and two neighbours in the sequence add to the next number. Watch for students who think the repeated three cannot be a sequence number.

video_script.why: The child fills a three row pyramid with the first three Virahanka Fibonacci numbers at the bottom, as the first pyramids of the chapter were filled, and checks the grid against the sequence.
video_script.substitution: Fill the middle row and the top by adding neighbours, then check each number of the grid against the sequence.
video_script.anchor: a bottom row card 1 2 3 and the start of the sequence 1, 2, 3, 5
video_script.payoff_line: The grid holds one, two, three, three, five and eight, and all are Virahanka Fibonacci numbers.

final_answer.value: 1, 2, 3, 3, 5 and 8; the top is 8; all are Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers
final_answer.spoken: the grid holds one, two, three, three, five and eight, and all are Virahanka Fibonacci numbers

maths_rules: Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ... each is the sum of the two before it.
The grid holds 1, 2, 3, 3, 5, 8; each of 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 is in the sequence.
video_script.design: One idea: neighbours add up the pyramid and in the sequence. The bottom row card stays in the anchor band and each row sits on the working board.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>What does the rest of the pyramid look like?

narration: <bookmark mark='top'/>Step two, the top is three plus five, which is eight.
